title: MZ Pushing a rock into a wall causes the playtest game to freeze-what should I do?

posts.author: string249
posts.body:
Hi all. Noob hobbyist here looking to try RPG Maker MZ and make a game for fun. This is probably nothing compared to the projects and troubleshooting that everyone's posted here, but I'm a bit stuck on something quite basic.
I'm following the in-built tutorials just to get a feel of the engine, and I reached step 10, the one about pushing boulders (Event application 2). I've followed the steps fine, but I've ran into a problem; pushing the rock into a wall or any surface with collision causes the playtest to freeze and stop running. I can't move or exit to menu and the only way to "fix" this is to close the playtest.
I've played around with the "skip if cannot move", and "wait for completion" boxes on the commands for both the rock and the player but no matter what combination of ticks or no-ticks I do, this always seems to persist.
What am I doing wrong? Is this a bug? Any way to fix this at all?
Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Yeah so both moveroutes have no "Skip if can not move" and "Wait for completion", so the game tries to let the boulder move into a wall, which is obviously not passable and you're telling it to wait until the boulder is inside the wall, which will never happen, making it so you will never be able to move, open the menu, or do anything else.
Also not sure why the boulder has a direction fix ON when the first thing you do is turning direction fix OFF when touching it.

As
@SGHarlekin
said, you need to check the “skip if cannot move” box; otherwise, the game will keep trying to force the action over and over.
And you need to uncheck the “fixed direction” box for the rock because, anyway, when you touch it with your character, it switches to “fixed direction off,” so you might as well just never enable it...
As for the “player's forward step,” I find it strange as a player to see my character follow the rock even though I'm no longer pressing the directional key.
In my opinion, you shouldn’t have the player follow it
(in Pokémon, the trainer doesn’t move once they’ve moved the rock; they have to take another step to move it again)
Test both versions and use the one you like best, of course

Just chiming in with an opposite opinion. Unless your game is built entirely around the mechanic of pushing things, I prefer the player to follow the thing pushed, like you've done. 99.999% of the time you're going to follow it anyway to push it further, and the player already pressed the directional key to initiate the push.
If your game
is
built entirely around the mechanic of pushing things, I'd say you should base it on how long the directional key was pressed – short tap to push without moving, otherwise push and move. This might boil down to not having a forward step (because if your key is still held the player will move anyway), but I'm not sure.
